emergencyNumber: No centralized emergency number. Contact local police or hospital directly.
healthcareSystem: Extremely limited public healthcare. Hospital Nacional Simao Mendes in Bissau is the main facility but suffers chronic shortages of staff, equipment, and medication. Rural areas have minimal health posts. Most serious cases require evacuation to Dakar, Senegal or Lisbon, Portugal.
qualityNotes: Healthcare quality is very poor. Facilities lack basic supplies and reliable electricity. Portuguese is the official language but many staff speak only Crioulo. Foreign patients should seek evacuation for anything beyond basic treatment.
pharmacyHours: Pharmacies in Bissau open 8am-6pm weekdays, 8am-1pm Saturday. Virtually no pharmacies outside the capital.
pharmacyTips: Very few pharmacies exist, almost all in Bissau. Medication supply is unreliable and counterfeit drugs are a serious concern. Bring all necessary medications from home. Portuguese is needed for pharmacy interactions.
prescriptionRules: Prescription enforcement is minimal. Availability is the main barrier — most medications are simply unavailable. Bring all needed medications with documentation in Portuguese if possible.

restrictedMeds.name: Narcotic medications
restrictedMeds.note: Carry a doctor's letter in Portuguese. Keep medications in original packaging.

bringDocumentation: Carry a doctor's letter listing all medications, ideally translated into Portuguese. Keep medications in original labeled packaging. Bring generous extra supplies as replacements are unavailable.

travelInsurance.tips: Comprehensive travel insurance with medical evacuation coverage is absolutely essential. Evacuation to Dakar or Lisbon can cost $30,000-100,000+. Ensure your policy covers conflict zones and has a 24-hour assistance line.

vaccinations.notes: Yellow fever vaccination is required for all travelers. Malaria is endemic throughout the country — prophylaxis is essential. Cholera outbreaks occur periodically.

waterNotes: Tap water is not safe to drink anywhere in Guinea-Bissau. Use only bottled or purified water for drinking and brushing teeth. Avoid ice unless you know it was made from purified water. Boil or treat water if bottled water is unavailable.
foodSafetyTips: Eat only thoroughly cooked food served hot. Avoid raw salads, unpeeled fruits, and street food unless freshly prepared. Seafood and rice dishes from reputable restaurants are safer options. Be cautious with dairy products.
medicalTourismNote: Guinea-Bissau is not a medical tourism destination. Patients requiring specialist care are evacuated to Dakar (Senegal), Lisbon (Portugal), or other European capitals.

hospitals.notes: Government facility. Limited English. Bring a translator app.

dentalCare.availability: Extremely limited. Only basic dental care available in Bissau.
dentalCare.notes: Dental facilities are very basic. There are very few trained dentists in the country. Bring dental emergency supplies.
dentalCare.emergencyTip: For dental emergencies, the national hospital may provide basic extraction. Evacuation to Dakar is recommended for anything complex.

mentalHealth.crisisLine: No dedicated mental health crisis line
mentalHealth.notes: Mental health services are virtually nonexistent. There are very few trained mental health professionals in the country. Consider telehealth services or evacuation if needed.

accessibilityInfo.overview: Accessibility infrastructure is extremely limited throughout Guinea-Bissau.
accessibilityInfo.hospitalAccess: Hospitals lack wheelchair ramps and accessible facilities.
accessibilityInfo.transport: No accessible public transport. Roads are unpaved and difficult to navigate.
accessibilityInfo.tips: Travelers with mobility needs should arrange private transport and consider whether the infrastructure can support their requirements before visiting.

covidStatus.entryRequirements: No COVID testing or vaccination requirements for entry as of 2026.
covidStatus.testing: Very limited COVID testing availability. Main hospitals in Bissau may offer testing.
covidStatus.notes: Healthcare capacity for COVID treatment is extremely limited.

insuranceClaimProcess: Obtain itemized receipts in Portuguese from any provider. Most facilities require cash payment upfront. Save all documentation for reimbursement claims with your insurer. Contact your insurance assistance line before seeking care if possible.

commonCosts.note: Costs are low but facilities are extremely basic. Cash payment expected. Private clinics charge more but offer marginally better care.

medicalEvacuation.note: Medical evacuation is essential for any serious condition. Ensure insurance covers air ambulance. Evacuation to Dakar is fastest; Lisbon offers the best Portuguese-speaking care.
